name: tpl-chain-response-1-goal
task: Carry the box to the exit. Whenever the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: 'Carry the box to the exit' is captured by the hard Existence(at_exit) plus the hard Response(at_exit, holding_box), which requires holding the box at the exit step (at_exit is last-step-only, so the consequent closes exactly when the box is held there). 'Whenever the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move' is correctly ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) hard: a fall empties the hands, so holding_box true on the very next step means the pickup happened then, and the environment guarantees a fall never occurs on the episode's last step, so the demand is always checkable. All three clauses are hard as worded (no preference cues), every clause traces to a task sentence, no redundant Existence is present (holding_box and box_fell are correctly not goals), and the machine's final state u3 requires the exit with the box while breaks of the chain lead to the rejecting state.

texts: At the exit, be holding the box.
Whenever the box falls, pick it up again on the very next step.
